messages.text:
I have an idea, we'll writing article and put the images of result. that i'll not break the law right ? 

so, i'd like to send the email to fastwork.com for ask permission for publish the website and source code for educational. 

and i'll put the link that deploy on vercel and lock with single password hash that contain in the vercel server no need database. and add this website to attachment. 

i'd like to ask you for research can we to the website likes this ?

Asking Fastwork for permission first is the right move. A researcher is now checking the legal side and the Vercel setup with sources; I'll reply here with its findings in about 20 min.
- Law: I'm not a lawyer. Thai and US copyright law both allow some use for study, criticism and review, but that is what the researcher is checking, with citations. Until then, treat it as unconfirmed.
- Lower-risk article: our own result images, charts and short clips, a credit to Fastwork, no logo use, and a note that we're not affiliated.
- Higher-risk: publishing the whole site copy or its source code. That is Fastwork's property, so it needs their written OK.
- Vercel without a database is possible in principle: a small server check of one password against a hash. The researcher is confirming which Vercel plan allows it.
- Our standing rule: nothing from this project goes online (no push, no deploy) until Fastwork says yes in writing and you then type "yes, prepare the public source copy".
- I can draft the email for you to send yourself. We never send email for you.
What you need to do: nothing now. Wait for the research reply here, then decide on the email.

I'd like to do the private website with single password hash first. i'll add in the email attachment for they can review the real result. (the optimize website could remove the script that contain the tracking and any observation)

Yes: I'm starting the private site now, built and tested on this Mac only; putting it online stays your step.
- Build: the v10 smooth version, with every tracking script removed (Amplitude, Hotjar, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Insights).
- Lock: one password hash in a Vercel setting, checked on every file, plus a "noindex" header so search engines skip it.
- Password: you pick it and run a small script that prints only the hash; we never see or store the password.
- Test: run locally first. Without the password every file must be refused; with it, the page must match v10.
- Online: our rule needs you to type "yes, prepare the public source copy" before any upload. You then deploy from your own Vercel account.
- Risk to weigh: the research could not settle whether a password link sent to Fastwork counts as "public". Sending clips first and the link after their reply is the safer order.
- Timing: the build is ready in about 1 h. If v10 changes before it lands, I rebuild it.
What you need to do: nothing now. When the build is ready, I'll post the steps here.
Can you start the local server and ask me for testing.

The demo server is running on this Mac, and your test step is on the console (C-080).
- Open http://localhost:5731/ in a Mac browser. The iPhone is mid-test, so don't use it.
- Without the password you should see only a sign-in box. Any user name works with the test password shown in C-080.
- The server stops by itself after 2 hours, and the password changes on every restart.
What you need to do: run C-080, then press Done with any notes.

Thanks, the local test passed (C-080: looks good).
- v10 may still change before it lands: the page-load fix (I-219) and fix B's first-open fix. If it does, I rebuild the demo from the final v10 and you test once more.
- The local server keeps running until about 09:37Z in case you want another look.
What you need to do: when you want it online, type "yes, prepare the public source copy" here. Then I post your upload steps.
What's the next step for deploy on vercel ?

no, need to prepare the source at this time. i'd like waiting the v10 done. 
i just would like to know how to deploy for information

Understood: nothing gets prepared now; we wait for v10. For your information, the deploy works like this:
- Password: pick 16+ random characters, then run "node hash-password.mjs" in the demo folder. It asks for the password without showing it and prints 2 values (a salt and a hash).
- Project: in a terminal in the demo folder, run "npx vercel@latest link" to create a new project under your account, never from git.
- Settings: add the 2 values as Sensitive environment variables (DEMO_PASS_SALT, DEMO_PASS_SHA256) in Project > Settings.
- Login wall: turn OFF "Vercel Authentication" under Deployment Protection, so Fastwork sees our password box, not a Vercel login.
- Upload: run "npx vercel@latest deploy --prod".
- Check: the link must ask for the password; with it, the page must look like v10.
- Afterwards: send the link and the password in separate messages; delete the project after Fastwork replies.
- The free Hobby plan is enough (non-commercial use).
What you need to do: nothing now. When v10 is done, I rebuild the demo and ask you to test it again.
Can we do the vercel config on this project ? i'd not create new project.

Yes, both readings are possible. Which one do you mean: (a) reuse a Vercel project you already have, or (b) deploy straight from this repo folder?
- (a) An existing Vercel project: link the demo folder to it ("vercel link", then choose that project). The upload replaces what that project serves now, and its password and login-wall settings apply.
- (b) From this repo: the Vercel config already lives here (research/private-demo/). Deploying from the repo root needs a strict allow-list, so only the demo files go up. Without it, the upload would also send site/, fixes/ and out/.
- Never from git in either case: our rule forbids pushing this repo to GitHub, so the upload is always the Vercel command, never a git connection.
- My recommendation: (a) if you have a spare project, or (b) with an allow-list. With (b), I'd run a dry upload list first and show it to you before any real upload.
What you need to do: reply "a" or "b". Nothing happens until v10 is done and you type the public-copy phrase.

Noted: (b), deploy straight from this repo folder with the Vercel command, never through git. I'll set it up after v10 is done, as you asked.
- Root files: a Vercel config and the password check at the repo root. The demo files go in one gitignored folder.
- Allow-list: a Vercel ignore file that blocks everything except those few files, so site/, fixes/, out/ and our logs never upload.
- Private ids: the ".vercel" folder that "vercel link" creates holds your account and project ids, so it gets added to .gitignore.
- Before the real upload: a script prints the exact upload list, you check it, and only then you deploy.
What you need to do: nothing now. When v10 is done, I post the upload list for your check, and then the phrase decides.

Correction: the local demo server stopped at 08:07Z, not 09:37Z as I said. My background job had a 30-min limit.
- Nothing is lost; the demo files are unchanged. I'll start it again whenever you want another look (it also frees your browser and the Mac for the timing checks).
What you need to do: nothing; just ask here if you want the demo back.
